trials.hypothesis: A 64-byte AVX-512BW pass can replace most per-byte control flow on large inputs: classify ASCII, continuations, and valid lead-byte ranges into masks; compare continuation lanes with the lead-derived sequence mask; enforce E0/ED/F0/F4 second-byte limits; and carry sequence requirements across blocks. A scalar tail and fallback preserve correctness where vectorization is unavailable. The baseline is about 49.55 µs, but no candidate result is available yet.

retained: Added a GCC x86 function-scoped AVX-512F/BW implementation guarded by runtime feature checks, without changing compiler flags or the run ABI.
Classified byte lanes into UTF-8 classes, verified lead/continuation sequence masks and special second-byte bounds, and carried continuation plus special-byte requirements across 64-byte blocks.
Restricted vector loads to complete 64-byte blocks and validated the carry-aware remainder with overflow-safe scalar length checks; retained scalar fallback for unsupported targets.

trials.hypothesis: An explicit scalar state machine that processes each byte once and tracks both remaining continuation bytes and the permitted interval for the next byte may avoid the existing parser's per-codepoint lookahead and length checks on valid mixed-width input. The per-byte state dispatch could also cost more, so no speedup is assumed.

retained: Validate UTF-8 by tracking the remaining continuation count and the legal interval for the next byte.
Constrain first continuation bytes for E0, ED, F0, and F4 to reject overlong encodings, surrogates, and code points above U+10FFFF.
Accept only when the input ends with no outstanding continuation bytes.

trials.hypothesis: Skipping complete native-width words proven ASCII may reduce byte-at-a-time overhead on long ASCII runs. Mixed-width inputs may have short runs, so word checks could instead add overhead; compare directly with the valid baseline (baseline-e1, mean 49.55 µs over three samples). The first word containing any non-ASCII byte is reprocessed from its beginning by the scalar validator, which also handles the tail and sequences crossing word boundaries.

retained: Scan only complete in-bounds uintptr_t-sized blocks, loading each with memcpy and skipping it only when every byte's high bit is clear.
Stop word scanning at the first mixed block without advancing its index; run the scalar UTF-8 validator from that block's beginning through the safely handled tail.
Use remaining-length checks for multibyte sequences to avoid boundary overreads.

trials.hypothesis: The current DFA performs a byte-class lookup followed by a state/class transition lookup for each byte. Folding those into a compile-time-generated state-by-raw-byte table should remove one dependent lookup while retaining a scalar, branch-light loop; the 2.5 KiB table may offset that benefit. The generated transitions also keep two continuation bytes outstanding after every valid first continuation of a four-byte sequence. Expect either a lower time on the 65,536-byte valid mixed-width workload or no gain if the larger table costs more. Stop immediately on any correctness failure; otherwise stop this variant if comparable repeated measurements do not beat the parent's 4.8878859e-05 s mean.

retained: Fold byte classification and state transitions into one compile-time-generated 10-by-256 raw-byte DFA lookup.
Correct four-byte lead transitions so valid first continuation bytes leave two continuation bytes outstanding.
Retain scalar per-byte processing, end-state acceptance, ABI, output behavior, and thread budget.

code_findings.mechanism: Si la voie AVX-512 est active, le carry paraît encoder incorrectement les continuations dues après une frontière de 64 octets. Un leader de 3 octets au lane 63 produit carry=2, alors que les positions 0 et 1 du bloc suivant doivent être des continuations. De plus, le traitement de queue rejette tout carry dont le bit 0 est nul. Il peut donc rejeter des séquences valides traversant la frontière, notamment E2 82 AC au lane 63 et F0 9F 98 80 aux lanes 62 ou 63. C’est une déduction du code, pas un échec de test observé.

Le code isole les intrinsics dans une fonction ciblée AVX-512F/BW, vérifie ces capacités à l’exécution et revient au validateur scalaire sinon. Les chargements vectoriels sont limités aux blocs complets de 64 octets; la queue est traitée séparément. run conserve l’ABI demandée, écrit un uint32 et ne lance pas de travail parallèle.

Un bloc ASCII avec une continuation en attente prend donc le chemin complet. La queue reste bornée par la longueur et passe ensuite au validateur scalaire; le dispatch et la signature run sont conservés. Le raccourci évite les comparaisons, pas le chargement ni le calcul du masque.
